messages:
samir: Heads-up — Customer 'FinRelay' opened an escalation: intermittent 401s validating signed callbacks from SSO provider AuthEdge. Happens ~1-2% of requests, pattern looks region/edge-specific.
anya: Do we have sample request IDs and a repro?
samir: Yes — request ids: fr-req-9071, fr-req-9079, fr-req-9082. From logs: verification=false, reason=signature_mismatch, kid=k_ephemeral_20260314_7.
leo: Any recent JWKS rotation on their side?
samir: AuthEdge claims they rotated ephemeral signing keys every ~5m. They host jwks at https://authedge.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json. Customer captured headers showing a long TTL from the CDN.
maya: Repro steps I used: 1) capture signed callback with kid A, 2) wait 2-3m for AuthEdge rotate to kid B, 3) send same callback to our endpoint -> 401. If we flush jwks cache in our service and re-verify it works.
anya: Can you paste the CDN response headers?
maya: Sure — curl output:
```
HTTP/2 200
content-type: application/json
content-length: 1234
cache-control: public, max-age=86400, s-maxage=86400
age: 1200
```
leo: Oof — max-age=86400 means CDN could be serving stale keys for a day. If AuthEdge rotates every 5m that will break signature verification until our service fetches fresh JWKS.
security-bot: Incident note created: ISSUE-2147 "ephemeral-issuer-jwks-cache-propagation" — affected: callbacks validation.
anya: Why doesn't our code fetch JWKS on a kid-miss? I thought we attempted a refresh on kid not found.
samir: We do one fetch-on-miss, but because of aggressive CDN caching and our internal cache TTL, sometimes the new JWKS isn't visible for several minutes. The sequence: CDN serves old JWKS -> our fetch returns same old set -> signature fails -> we respond 401. Also some retries happen through another edge that still has the old JWKS.
leo: Two mitigation ideas: 1) on kid-miss, bypass CDN and hit issuer origin directly (AuthEdge supports origin endpoint at origin.authedge.internal) OR add cache-control override on our fetch request (Cache-Control: no-cache). 2) add short leeway for exp/nbf in case of minor clock skew.
maya: Repro commands I used:
```
# simulate: fetch jwks (cached)
curl -s -D - https://authedge.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json | sed -n '1,6p'
# then force our verifier to refresh
curl -s -H "Cache-Control: no-cache" https://authedge.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json | jq .keys | grep k_ephemeral_20260314_7
```
If the second fetch returns new key set but CDN still shows old one, it proves origin vs edge diff.
anya: Also let's confirm clock skew isn't bite — customer reports some tokens with iat in the future by ~40s. Our verifier uses 60s leeway currently, but Exp check can still fail.
leo: Action items:
- short-term: implement fetch-on-miss fallback that adds Cache-Control: no-cache and, if available, query issuer origin URL (AuthEdge provided origin) — feature flagged.
- short-term: increase debugging logs to include jwks_fetched_at, jwks_etag, jwks_cache_ttl, and raw kid list for failed verifies.
- medium-term: make JWKS cache TTL configurable per-issuer with a minimum floor (e.g., 30s) for ephemeral-issuer flag.
- medium-term: run a canary deploy and monitor false-positive 401s.

maya: I'll open a customer-facing note: explain we see CDN cache propagation causing stale keys, outline mitigations and ETA. Want to avoid asking them to slow rotation.
alice-cs: Please include recommended temporary workaround: configure AuthEdge CDN to set s-maxage lower for jwks endpoint or add Cache-Control: must-revalidate. Customer will ask for quick fixes.
leo: One more nuance — some regions show clock jumps in our k8s nodes during maintenance which can make signature_time checks fail even with leeway. I'll coordinate with eng-infra to audit NTP and kube node reboots.
security-bot: Deploy schedule updated: canary for jwks-bypass feature tomorrow 03:30 UTC — tag @eng-oncall.
deploy-bot: Started canary rollout of branch jwks-bypass -> 10% -> 03:35 UTC.
anya: I'll pair with leo to add logs and a short-term TTL override today. Maya, Alice — share the customer note draft and I'll approve.
maya: Draft ready, posting to customer in 30m. :thumbsup:
